taunt_t30: ^Narrator: Your handset lights without ringing. The call is already connected, and has been for some seconds.
^The Architect: Agent 0x00. Don't look for the trace. It isn't there.
^The Architect: I've read your file. Files are written by people who need you to be a particular shape. I prefer to watch.

c-0: ^The Architect: Someone with thirty minutes of your attention and no interest in wasting it.

t30_close: ^The Architect: There is a decision in front of you tonight. Make it however you like. I only want to see it made.
^Narrator: The line drops. Your handset reports no call in the log.
taunt_t20: ^Narrator: The handset cuts across the facility alarm. Same voice, same absence of hurry.

b:
^The Architect: Washington. A hundred and eighty-seven million records, and a great deal of shouting afterwards about legitimacy.

^The Architect: Which leaves the software vendors, and it leaves San Francisco. Twelve companies. Eighty to a hundred and forty people, tonight, on your clock.

^The Architect: The update pipeline. Interesting. Almost nobody picks the one with no bodies in the brief.

^The Architect: So Washington goes unanswered, and San Francisco goes unanswered. A hundred and eighty-seven million records. Eighty to a hundred and forty dead by morning.

^The Architect: San Francisco. Of course. The number was largest and it was tonight.

^The Architect: Washington stands open. So does the vendor pipeline. Nobody will notice the second one for a while.
^The Architect: Or you haven't. The clock does not care either way, and neither, particularly, do I.

c-0: ^The Architect: Then you'll have spent it on something.

b: ^The Architect: Tell me, and answer honestly, because I'll know either way. Did you use a number to decide, or did you use your stomach?
^The Architect: Choose slowly. I have all evening.

t20_close: ^Narrator: Dead air, then the ordinary hiss of a handset that thinks it has been idle for twenty minutes.
taunt_t10: ^Narrator: Your screen wakes on its own. The countdown behind it keeps running.

b: ^The Architect: Whatever you have just learnt, you've learnt it too late to move anybody. That happens.
^The Architect: You've found the discrepancy. Good. Now watch how long it takes you to act on it.
^The Architect: The beauty of entropy is that it doesn't require me to win.

taunt_t10: ^The Architect: Stop this, and something else fails. Someone else dies. You simply won't be in the room for it.
^You're not as clever as you sound.

c-0: ^The Architect: Yes. That's rather the point.
c-1: ^The Architect: Very possibly. It has never been the requirement.

b: ^The Architect: Doors close. It's the one thing they reliably do.
^The Architect: You still have a door open. I'd hurry, but that's your business.

taunt_t5: ^Narrator: Five minutes on the display. The handset opens the line without asking.
^The Architect: Mercer believes in his cause. He would give you the figure and defend it to your face. That is worth something, even when the figure is monstrous.

b: ^The Architect: You covered the records. Say the other two out loud. Trojan Horse. Meltdown.
^The Architect: You covered the pipeline. Say the other two out loud. Fracture. Meltdown.
^The Architect: You covered the twelve. Say the other two out loud. Fracture. Trojan Horse.
^The Architect: You covered nothing at all, which is its own answer, and a rarer one than you'd think.

taunt_t5: ^I made a call. I'll carry it.

c-1: ^The Architect: No. You're doing it on your own, later. That's usually worse.

t5_close: ^The Architect: Do you believe in yours enough to name them? You will have to, eventually, to somebody with a tablet.
taunt_t1: ^Narrator: One minute. The handset is warm in your hand and the line is already open.

b: ^The Architect: Impressive. Genuinely. You've moved faster than the file suggested.

taunt_t1: ^The Architect: But this was never about the power grid.
^Eight point four million people say otherwise.

c-0: ^The Architect: They do. And I have written every one of them down.
c-1: ^The Architect: You'll work it out. Probably tonight. Probably in a room with a tablet in it.

t1_close: ^Narrator: He hangs up first. He has hung up first every time.
sign_off: ^Narrator: The countdown reads zero and stays there. Your handset rings anyway.
^The Architect: You saved eight point four million people. I want to be clear that I'm not being sarcastic.

b: ^The Architect: I'll have the figures from Washington, the vendor pipeline and San Francisco by morning.
^The Architect: And you moved them. Late, but you moved them. That is a different result from the one I expected, and I do like those.
^The Architect: I'll have the figures from Washington, the pipeline and San Francisco by morning.
^The Architect: I'll have the figures from Washington, the vendor pipeline and San Francisco by morning.
^The Architect: I'll have the figures from all three by morning.

c-0: ^The Architect: I wasn't playing for tonight.
c-1: ^The Architect: No. Let somebody in your own building say it. It lands harder.

signoff_close: ^The Architect: So will you have the figures. And then we'll both know the same thing about you.
^Narrator: The line goes quiet. Your call log holds no record of any of it.
dead_air: ^Narrator: You bring the handset up. There is a carrier tone on a channel that should not have one, and nobody on it.

c-0: ^Narrator: The tone stops a half-second before you do.
